title: Unitree’s IPO could value China’s robot champion at $7bn or more
excerpt: Sponsor CITIC says Unitree could be worth over 50 billion yuan after its Shanghai listing, a milestone for China’s humanoid-robot leader as demand accelerates.
content_html:
China’s best-known robot maker is about to test the public markets. Unitree could be worth more than 50 billion yuan, roughly $7bn, after its Shanghai listing, according to its IPO sponsor.The estimate comes from CITIC Securities.

As the deal’s sponsor, CITIC set out the valuation as Unitree kicked off pricing for its float on Shanghai’s STAR Market, the exchange’s board for technology companies.Some readings run higher still. Depending on where the shares price, other estimates suggest the valuation could climb well above that figure, a sign of how much appetite there is for the stock.

The timing plays to the hype. Unitree says it expects revenue to grow in the first half of the year as demand for humanoid robots accelerates, giving the listing a genuine growth story to sell.

Unitree made its name on price. It builds both four-legged robots and humanoids, and undercut Western rivals dramatically, putting a walking humanoid within reach of universities, developers and even hobbyists.

That affordability reshaped the field. By pricing its machines far below competitors, Unitree turned humanoid robots from lab curiosities into products people could actually buy, seeding a developer base around its hardware.

The listing is also a milestone for its home market. It follows the recent approval of Unitree’s Shanghai listing registration, clearing the last big hurdle before the shares reach investors.

Beijing has a stake in the outcome. China has designated humanoid robotics a strategic priority, and a marquee domestic IPO is exactly the kind of showcase the government wants as it races the United States in physical AI.

Unitree is not the only one going public. Rivals are lining up too, with humanoid maker EngineAI filing for a Hong Kong IPO, a wave of listings that signals the sector’s move from prototype to profit.

Demand is showing up in unexpected places. China’s carmakers are among the buyers, with BYD planning to put a humanoid robot in its showrooms, a concrete use case that helps justify the valuations.

The software is catching up to the hardware. Systems such as Google DeepMind’s Gemini Robotics models now control whole humanoids, narrowing the gap between a machine that walks and one that is genuinely useful.

The choice of venue matters. Listing on Shanghai’s STAR Market keeps a strategic company on a domestic exchange, in line with Beijing’s preference for keeping its technology champions and their capital at home.

The race with the United States hangs over the deal. American firms are pouring money into humanoids too, and a well-funded, publicly listed Unitree gives China a flagship to point to in a contest it frames as central to the future.

Still, the enthusiasm carries risk. Humanoid robots remain expensive to build and unproven at scale, and a rich IPO valuation bakes in an assumption that mass adoption arrives faster than it so far has.

Unitree’s numbers will face scrutiny once it is public. Growth expectations are one thing, but listed companies must show durable revenue, and a young hardware firm carries the volatility that comes with a new market.

The valuation range itself tells a story. That estimates swing from around 50 billion yuan to twice that reflects how little agreement there is on what a humanoid-robot maker is actually worth this early.

For now, the float is a statement of intent. A $7bn-plus valuation would crown Unitree as the standard-bearer for China’s robot ambitions, and set a benchmark the rest of the industry will be measured against.

content_html_zh:
中国最著名的机器人制造商即将试水公开市场。 据其 IPO 保荐人称，Unitree 在上海上市后的估值可能超过 500 亿元人民币（约合 70 亿美元）。这一估计来自中信证券。

作为本次交易的发起人，中信集团在 Unitree 开始在上海科创板（科技公司的交易所主板）上市定价时公布了估值。一些读数仍在走高。 其他估计表明，根据股价的走势，估值可能会远高于该数字，这表明对该股的兴趣有多大。

时机恰逢炒作。 Unitree 表示，随着对人形机器人的需求加速，预计今年上半年的收入将增长，从而为上市提供真正的增长故事。

Unitree 因价格而出名。 它制造了四足机器人和人形机器人，并大幅削弱了西方竞争对手，使大学、开发人员甚至业余爱好者都能够接触到行走的人形机器人。

这种负担能力重塑了这个领域。 通过将其机器定价远低于竞争对手，Unitree 将人形机器人从实验室的好奇心变成了人们可以实际购买的产品，围绕其硬件培育了开发者基础。

此次上市对于其本土市场来说也是一个里程碑。 此前，UniTree在上海的上市注册已于近期获得批准，扫清了股票到达投资者手中的最后一大障碍。

结果对北京有利害关系。 中国已将仿人机器人技术列为战略重点，而大规模的国内首次公开募股正是中国政府在物理人工智能领域与美国展开竞争时所希望的展示。

Unitree并不是唯一一家上市的公司。 竞争对手也在排队，人形机器人制造商 EngineAI 申请了香港 IPO，这一波上市标志着该行业从原型转向盈利。

需求出现在意想不到的地方。 中国汽车制造商是买家之一，比亚迪计划在其展厅中放置一个人形机器人，这是一个有助于证明估值合理性的具体用例。

软件正在赶上硬件。 谷歌 DeepMind 的 Gemini Robotics 模型等系统现在可以控制整个类人机器人，缩小了行走机器与真正有用的机器之间的差距。

场地的选择很重要。 在上海科创板上市可以让一家战略公司留在国内交易所，这符合北京方面将其技术龙头企业及其资本留在国内的偏好。

与美国的竞争仍悬而未决。 美国公司也在向人形机器人投入大量资金，而资金雄厚、公开上市的 Unitree 为中国在这场对未来至关重要的竞争中提供了一个旗舰。

尽管如此，这种热情也存在风险。 人形机器人的制造成本仍然很高，而且尚未得到大规模验证，而高额的 IPO 估值则让人假设大规模采用的速度比迄今为止更快。

Unitree 的数据一旦公开将面临审查。 增长预期是一回事，但上市公司必须表现出持久的收入，而一家年轻的硬件公司会承受新市场带来的波动。

估值范围本身就讲述了一个故事。 这一估计在 500 亿元人民币左右到两倍之间波动，这反映出人们对于仿人机器人制造商的实际价值如此早达成的共识是多么的少。

目前，浮动只是一种意向声明。 超过 70 亿美元的估值将使 Unitree 成为中国机器人雄心的旗手，并为行业其他公司设定衡量基准。
